newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian PM resigns in row over Finance Ministry.
newsitem.headline: Latvian PM resigns in row over Finance Ministry.

text.p: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele, bowing to a public storm over the appointment of a new minister, said on Monday he had handed in his resignation after just over a year in office.
His resignation letter to President Guntis Ulmanis followed a week of outcry about the appointment of Vassily Melnik, a 29-year-old Latvian businessman, as finance minister in the Baltic state.
Shkele said he was resigning after "the president and the political elite accused me of pressing upon them amoral decisions".

"I don't see a possibility of continuing to lead the government without the trust of both president and parliament following these irresponsible, totally groundless and too grave accusations," he said.
"I have done all within my power to secure the government's work but I have to conclude this task has proved to be too difficult," Shkele told a news conference.
"I am sad to leave a job successfully started but I am also satisfied that I am handing over the state to my successor in a much better condition than I received it. My conscience is clean."
The president was still considering the surprise resignation and no decision had yet been made.
"We have received the statement 20 minutes ago. As soon there is a decision we will inform you," a spokeswoman for the president told Reuters.
Shkele's resignation followed a call by Ulmanis for members of parliament not to approval Melnik's appointment.
Local media alleged he was being investigated for a conflict of interest. The prosecutor's office later confirmed the report but said it had found no breach of anti-corruption laws.
Melnik, however, was backed by parliament, winning 44 votes in favour of his appointment and with 24 voting against him. The rest of the 100 members were absent or did not vote.
The non-aligned Shkele, a well known entrepreneur, became prime minister in December 1995 after being asked by Ulmanis to form a new government.

Shkele was deputy agriculture minister when Latvia regained its independence from the former Soviet Union in 1991 and was chairman of the state-owned Latvian Shipping Company when he was appointed prime minister.
He was seen as a compromise premier with the potential to unite rival factions, after two proposed governments were voted down by parliament.
Shkele's aim was to make Latvia more investor-friendly and he was the country's first prime minister to successfully push through a balanced budget in 1997 last December.
He was currently proposing a two-year budget for 1998/99 to parliament to give longterm signals to businessmen.
